newsitem.title: USA: Intel more than doubled fourth-quarter profits. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Intel more than doubled fourth-quarter profits. [CORRECTED 23:30 GMT]

text.p: Intel Corp. reported Tuesday that its fourth-quarter profits more than doubled, reflecting strong sales of its popular Pentium and Pentium Pro microprocessors and exceeding analysts' predictions.

The world's largest semiconductor maker said it earned $1.9 billion, or $2.13 a share, in the last three months of 1996, up from $867 million, or 98 cents a share, a year ago. Revenues rose to $6.4 billion from $4.58 billion.
Wall Street analysts on average had expected the company to report fourth-quarter earnings equal to $1.84 per share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.

The Santa Clara, Calif.-based semiconductor giant said it earned $5.2 billion, or $5.81 per share, in all of 1996, compared with earnings of $3.6 billion, or $4.03 a share, in 1995. Intel generated $20.8 billion in revenues last year, a 29 percent increase from 1995's $16.2 billion.
The report marked the seventh year in a row of record revenues and earnings for Intel, the company said.
"Intel hit on all cylinders in 1996, the 25th anniversary of the introduction of the microprocessor," Intel Chief Executive Andrew Grove said in a statement.

Intel, which issued its earnings report after markets closed, was the most actively traded share on Nasdaq Tuesday, with more than 14 million shares changing hands. The stock ended up 25 cents at $147.125, a 52-week high.
The company announced a two-for-one stock split along with its results.
Intel, which provides the microprocessors used in 80 percent of the world's computers, is widely regarded as a bellwether for the personal computer group.

"Fueling demand in 1996 were a number of factors, including the continued growth of the Internet, the rapid penetration of PCs into emerging markets, especially in Asia, the beginnings of a corporate computing upgrade cycle and the increasing role the PC plays as a communications device," Grove said.
Intel said it expected first-quarter 1997 revenues to hit about $6.4 billion vs. $4.64 billion in the year-ago quarter.
